14 A uniform rod of length 200 cm is freely pivoted at point P. The rod is held horizontally in
equilibrium by a 60 N weight that is attached to the rod by a string passing over a frictionless
pulley.
string
frictionless
pulley
uniform rod
40 cm
30°
P
200 cm
weight
60 N
What is the weight of the rod?
A
30 N
B
60 N
C
80 N
D
140 N

hints: Notice the pivot P is $40 \text{ cm}$ from the left end of the $200 \text{ cm}$ rod, so find how far the centre of mass and the right-hand end are from P.

The string tension is $60 \text{ N}$ because of the $60 \text{ N}$ weight and frictionless pulley, but it pulls at $30^{\circ}$ to the horizontal, so only the vertical part $T \sin 30^{\circ}$ lifts the rod.
Set the clockwise moment of the rod weight about P equal to the anticlockwise moment of that vertical $30 \text{ N}$ pull and solve for the rod weight.
walkthrough: The uniform rod is $200 \text{ cm}$ long, so its weight $W$ acts at its midpoint, $100 \text{ cm}$ from the left end. Pivot P is $40 \text{ cm}$ from the left end, so $W$ acts $100 - 40 = 60 \text{ cm}$ to the right of P and produces a clockwise moment.
The right-hand end where the string is attached is $200 - 40 = 160 \text{ cm}$ to the right of P. The frictionless pulley means string tension $T = 60 \text{ N}$.
Only the vertical component of this angled pull can exert a moment about the horizontal rod. It is $T_v = T \sin 30^{\circ} = 60 \times 0.5 = 30 \text{ N}$ upwards, giving an anticlockwise moment.
For horizontal equilibrium the principle of moments about P gives sum of clockwise moments = sum of anticlockwise moments: $W \times 60 \text{ cm} = 30 \text{ N} \times 160 \text{ cm}$.
Hence $W = 4800 / 60 = 80 \text{ N}$. This is option C.

A.explanation: This is only the vertical component $60 \sin 30^{\circ} = 30 \text{ N}$ of the string tension, not the rod weight after balancing moments about P.

B.explanation: This assumes the $60 \text{ N}$ tension balances the rod weight directly, ignoring both the $30^{\circ}$ angle and the different distances from P.

C.explanation: Balancing moments about P gives $W \times 60 \text{ cm} = 30 \text{ N} \times 160 \text{ cm}$, so $W = 80 \text{ N}$.

D.explanation: This is too large and results from using the full $60 \text{ N}$ tension or the wrong lever arm instead of the $30 \text{ N}$ vertical component at $160 \text{ cm}$ from P.
